Header:
Date: 2026-02-18 | Start: 10:30 PST | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM); Sofia Lopez (AstraHealth CTO), Daniel Reed (ML Eng), Avery Chen (Infra), Marta Ruiz (Product)

--- Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete) ---
Redwood presented latest benchmark spreadsheet comparing Redwood runtime to AstraHealth's baseline provider. Main points: p50/p95 improvements on 8k token models for generation when using KV caching and batching; baseline provider shows slightly better single-request long-seq p99 in some runs. Discussed tuning (quantization, batch sizes, kernel selection), VPC networking for private tests, and next steps for another baseline run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright good morning everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have 45 minutes, we'll go through the benchmark results quickly and then open for q's.
[00:12] Sofia: morning, thanks Maya. We got the sheet, skimmed it but want walk through the differences, specifically p95 on the 4k vs 8k runs.
[00:25] Jonah: yeah cool, so quick context - this is the normalized run where we re-ran your sample traces with our runner, we used same model family you specified, 30 concurrent clients for throughput tests and varied batch sizes, and we turned on prefix kv-cache for the caching experiments.
[00:45] Daniel: small note, in our baseline runs we had a slightly different tokenization step, so numbers won't be 1:1 but should be close.
[00:53] Jonah: yep, that explains some of the micro-delta.
[01:10] Jonah: ok slide one, p50/p95 latency table — for short prompts (<=256 tokens) Redwood p95 is ~120ms vs baseline 220ms, p50 45ms vs 90ms. For 4k seq with kv caching we saw p95 ~480ms vs baseline ~620ms. For 8k sequence generation, baseline had a lower p99 in our one sustained run — we think that's due to their optimized kernel path for very long attention windows.
[01:42] Marta: can you repeat that - baseline better on long sequences? that's surprising given your caching claims.
[01:50] Jonah: yeah it's specific to the single-stream long sequence p99. Our batching + cache gives great throughput and lower median/p95 for mixed workloads. But in a sustained single-request long history case, baseline's implementation currently hits a slightly better p99 in this config — could be kernel selection and their fused-attn path.
[02:10] Sofia: okay makes sense. What about throughput numbers, tokens/sec?
[02:18] Jonah: tokens/sec — in the 8k test with 30 clients, Redwood sustained ~48k tokens/s across the pool, baseline ~30k tokens/s. When we enabled larger batch sizes and async batching the throughput increased to ~72k tokens/s in our best config.
[02:40] Daniel: did you do the run with quantized weights? we run int8 in prod sometimes.
[02:47] Jonah: we did a few runs with int8 and 4-bit for certain model variants — those had lower memory footprint and similar latency but slightly higher variance on tail in some cases. The numbers in the sheet are mixed; see the quantization tab for more details.
[03:05] Maya: quick practical note — the p95 reductions we show translate to cost savings because you get more throughput per GPU and fewer hot-path fallbacks. So for your throughput targets you should see ~30-40% lower GPU cost per token in our runs, depending on model and quantization.
[03:25] Sofia: that's compelling. Our CFO cares about that, but security questions are top of mind: SAML/SSO, KMS for keys, audit logs. Priya can you take notes?
[03:35] Priya: yep. We have SOC2 docs and KMS integration details; I'll attach in follow-up.
[03:40] Avery: another infra question - network egress and VPC peering might add latency. Did you test with VPC peering?
[03:47] Jonah: this run was in our hosted env without VPC peering; we did a separate private test with VPC peered cluster and saw a small bump (~10-20ms) due to networking depending on region. We'll share those logs.
[04:05] Marta: the sheet has a column called "normed latency" can you say how that's calculated?
[04:12] Jonah: sure, normalized latency is where we align tokenization and warmup sequences and remove cold-starts; basically we trim the first 5 tokens of each run and rebase to per-token average to make it comparable across provider traces.
[04:28] Sofia: filler question - what about throttling and rate limiting? we need predictable SLOs.
[04:35] Maya: Dedicated mode gives you reserved capacity and SLA guarantees; we also support burst with configurable autoscaling policies. Jonah can share typical autoscale configs we've used for similar customers.
[04:48] Jonah: example config: min reserved nodes + scaling up on queue length, warm pools for fast spin-up. We also have graceful fallback to smaller model variants if capacity constrained.
[05:02] Daniel: about that fallback: how do you ensure quality when switching models mid-stream?
[05:08] Jonah: great question — we recommend evaluation sets and a soft fallback where we re-score outputs on the edge and if below threshold we route to the higher-quality model; it's a configurable rollout policy in the console.
[05:22] Sofia: back to the numbers, I notice the baseline provider had one run where p99 spiked to 3s on 8k and your run was 1.8s, but another run flipped. Are these noise?
[05:33] Jonah: some variance is noise — we think the flips correlate with kernel selection and the underlying GPU memory pressure. In their run, garbage collection and host-to-device memory copies may have created the spike. We'll attach raw perf counters so you can correlate.
[05:48] Maya: action item — we'll send the normalized sheet plus raw logs including perf counters and kernel choices.
[05:55] Sofia: appreciated. A few procurement questions - pricing model comparison: baseline has a blended commit with overage, you said Redwood has usage + reserved options?
[06:05] Maya: yes hosted usage pricing per token, and Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity with monthly/annual commit discounts. We can show a sample TCO for your 3-month pilot vs Dedicated commit.
[06:18] Marta: any red flags on compliance? we need audit logs and key access controls.
[06:23] Priya: we support audit logs, role-based access controls, and integrations with customer KMS/HSM; I'll send a security pack after the call.
[06:33] Avery: one more infra nit - when you reported 72k tokens/s with async batching what batch sizes were you using?
[06:39] Jonah: typical beta config was batch size 64 with dynamic batching and async coalescing; for larger models we capped at 32 to avoid memory pressure. The sheet's batching tab has exact params per run.
[06:55] Daniel: can you also share the CLI commands you used to run the baseline to reproduce?
[07:00] Jonah: yes we'll include the runbook and script in the repo link.
[07:08] Sofia: ok timeline — we want to make final pilot decision by end of month, which gives us about two more weeks. We'll need the security docs and cost model to share with finance.
[07:18] Maya: understood. We'll prioritize the security pack and the normalized logs first.
[07:25] Daniel: quick technical: you mentioned your runtime uses kernel selection heuristics — can you give an example when it picks a different kernel?
[07:32] Jonah: sure — e.g., for models with causal attention and short sequence we pick a fused attention kernel that minimizes memory copies; for very long sequences we try an attention algorithm with streaming-friendly memory layout. The selection is based on seq length, batch size, and available GPU memory.
[07:50] Marta: do you support customer-managed keys for model weights in private deployments?
[07:55] Priya: yes, in Private + VPC you can integrate with your KMS/HSM so keys never leave your control. We'll send architecture note.
[08:03] Sofia: any blockers for us to run the extended baseline test with 2x sequence length?
[08:09] Jonas: sorry Jonas->Jonah: (laugh) yes we can help set that up but we need the peering window and a contact from your infra to coordinate. Avery?
[08:17] Avery: I'll open a peering window next Tues and share the details.
[08:21] Maya: perfect. We'll coordinate schedule by email.
[08:25] Daniel: one more small ask — can you include the tail-distribution plots rather than only p95? we want to see full CDF.
[08:31] Jonah: yes will attach CDF plots and raw samples.
[08:36] Sofia: when we review the spreadsheet with finance, what is the conservative TCO delta we should assume?
[08:42] Maya: conservative estimate: 20% cost saving at parity quality; typical is 30-40% depending on quantization and batching. We'll include both conservative and optimistic scenarios.
[08:55] Marta: ok good. procurement wise, if we decide Dedicated we'd need contract, SLAs, and a runbook for on-call.
[09:03] Priya: we have templates for that — can share an example SLA and SOW.
[09:09] Sofia: fine. Anything else?
[09:12] Daniel: not from me.
[09:13] Maya: ok recap of next steps: Maya send normalized spreadsheet+pricing (due 2/20), Jonah send runbook/kernels/CDF plots (2/22), Daniel run extended baseline (2/26), Avery confirm peering window (2/24), Priya send security pack (2/20). We'll schedule a follow-up after the extended baseline.
[09:35] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[09:36] Maya: thanks, bye.
